measured: Application calls and optional settings are recorded below at the cited commits.

applications.name: volter-ai/media
applications.client: plain fetch (Node 22) with Authorization: Bearer LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN, Linkedin-Version: 202609 and X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0 on every https://api.linkedin.com/rest call; the part PUTs carry no token

backend.call: POST /rest/videos?action=initializeUpload { initializeUploadRequest: { owner, fileSizeBytes, uploadCaptions: false, uploadThumbnail: false } }, reading value.uploadInstructions, value.video and value.uploadToken
PUT part.uploadUrl with each part's bytes (firstByte..lastByte), content-type application/octet-stream and no Authorization, reading the answer's etag
POST /rest/videos?action=finalizeUpload { finalizeUploadRequest: { video, uploadToken, uploadedPartIds: the etags in order } }
GET /rest/videos/{encodeURIComponent(video)} up to 30 times a second apart, until status is AVAILABLE; PROCESSING_FAILED stops the send

POST /rest/posts { author: urn:li:organization:100000001, commentary (little text, every reserved character escaped), visibility PUBLIC, distribution MAIN_FEED, lifecycleState PUBLISHED, isReshareDisabledByAuthor false, content.media { id, title } }, reading the x-restli-id header
every call's refusal: any status >= 400 is thrown with its body (a bad or expired token, a missing scope, an unknown version, a refused upload, the rate limit)
the token from LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN and the organization urn:li:organization:100000001 the send posts as, with the title 'Model Editor by VideoGame AI'

paste the campaign's LinkedIn copy, attach the horizontal render from his machine (Add media), and Post: the Videos API's initializeUpload, part uploads and finalizeUpload, then the Posts API's create; a photo through the Images API's

post as the page he administers from the same share box (Post as), and see the page's posts on its Posts tab
